plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Promotion name at this version. Keeps history of all versions' titles. Example: 'Black Friday Flash - V2'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Full snapshot of description at change time. Used for investigation/audit.

plainFields.name: rule_type
plainFields.description: Rule type as configured in parent promo at this snapshot point. Example: 'coupon'.

plainFields.name: active
plainFields.description: Whether this snapshot was active at time of edit. For operational and display audit. Example: true.

plainFields.name: starts_at
plainFields.description: Activation window start at this version. Used for rollback and forensic controls.

plainFields.name: ends_at
plainFields.description: End window as configured at last edit (nullable if open-ended).

plainFields.name: snapshot_at
plainFields.description: Time of snapshot record creation (mutation timestamp/audit trail).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Free-text log for what caused change (admin note, auto, backend, AI, etc). Used for audit, compliance, and forensic analysis.

models.name: ai_shopmall_ai_recommendations
models.description:
AI Recommendation results for users or sessions – Implements requirements from Analytics & AI Platform (requirementAnalysisReport, 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md).

Business purpose: Stores top-N recommendation outcomes for users or sessions, categorized by scenario (e.g., homepage, product detail, campaign promo). Maintains strict 3NF normalization; only atomic fields and references. Example: logs that user X received product Y and Z suggestions on date T, with ranking scores.

Key relationships: References analytic_profile or user via foreign keys (customer or seller, from Actors), and products (from Products domain). Behavioral constraints: Must not denormalize product/title or user info, and must always preserve recommendation reason and scoring.
Special behaviors: Each entry belongs to a computation cycle (e.g. nightly batch or real-time), can be audited per recommendation engine version.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each recommendation result.

foreignFields.name: analytic_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Target user or analytic profile’s {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_profiles.id}. Represents the subject entity to whom the recommendation was made.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Recommended product’s {@link ai_shopmall_products.id}. Points to a product in the master catalog.

plainFields.name: recommendation_type
plainFields.description: Type or scenario for the recommendation (e.g., homepage, cross-sell, upsell, campaign). Fully normalized single atomic value per record. Example: 'homepage', 'detail_page', 'email_campaign'.

plainFields.name: rank
plainFields.description: Ranking position of this product in the recommendation list (1 = highest). Atomic, required for repeatable evaluation.

plainFields.name: score
plainFields.description: Numeric score assigned by the recommendation engine (not pre-calculated rank, but model output only). E.g. affinity or predicted CTR.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Human-readable reason, label or short classifier for why the item was recommended (e.g., 'Similar to X', 'Best sellers', 'Based on cart'). Not calculated aggregation – single cause only.

plainFields.name: engine_version
plainFields.description: Version string of the recommendation model/algorithm that generated this entry. For audit and tracking. No aggregated summaries.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the recommendation was generated. Always required for auditability. Not aggregated.

models.name: ai_shopmall_fraud_activities
models.description:
Fraud detection events per Analytics & AI requirements (see 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md). Implements event-level abnormal/fraud activity logging for audits and intervention triggers.

Business purpose: Captures suspicious activities/transactions flagged by the AI fraud engine or anomaly detectors. Maintains 3NF: one record per unique activity/event per scan. Example: logs when an order is detected with abnormal purchase velocity or flagged as synthetic. Not a pre-calculated aggregate. No duplicate/roll-up fields allowed.

Key relationships: References analytic_event, user (from Actors), or entity IDs. Used by admins for incident review.
Special behaviors: Each entry is immutable for compliance and audit purposes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each fraud activity event.

foreignFields.name: analytic_event_id
foreignFields.description: Related event’s {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_events.id}. Connects this fraud incident to the originating analytic event record.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: Optionally links to a user (customer, seller, admin) who triggered the activity. References {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}, ai_shopmall_sellers.id, or ai_shopmall_administrators.id as needed. Kept fully normalized; only a single user reference per activity.

plainFields.name: activity_type
plainFields.description: Type/category of detected fraud or anomaly (e.g., payment_fraud, fake_review, velocity_attack, account_takeover). Atomic value only. No aggregated patterns.

plainFields.name: context_info
plainFields.description: Optional JSON or text describing the context/details of the fraud activity detected. E.g., device info, IP, AI model findings. Single event context only, not an aggregation.

plainFields.name: detected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of fraud detection. Required, atomic and non-aggregated per row. UTC datetime only.

plainFields.name: is_escalated
plainFields.description: If this fraud activity was escalated for manual or admin review. Not pre-calculated rollup – atomic per event.

models.name: ai_shopmall_analytic_events
models.description:
Raw analytic event log for Analytics & AI Platform. See requirements from analytic_events entity in 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md.

Business purpose: Logs all fine-grained, atomic user or system events for subsequent AI analysis, insight dashboards, or real-time triggers. Examples: product_view, add_to_cart, purchase, page_visit, recommendation_clicked. 

Strict 3NF: Each record logs a single discrete event. Contains NO aggregates/summaries.
Key relationships: References analytic_profile, may reference user or related objects by ID only.
Special behaviors: Immutable; never roll up, summarize, or denormalize within this table.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each analytic event.

foreignFields.name: analytic_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Subject’s {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_profiles.id}. Identifies user/session/actor for this event. Required, atomic.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Atomic type of analytic event (e.g., product_view, add_to_cart, checkout, order_complete). No rollups. Business event only.

plainFields.name: event_data
plainFields.description: Raw event payload, typically structured JSON or key-value string form. Must only include atomic event data for this row; never summary forms. For example: product_id, page, metadata.

plainFields.name: occurred_at
plainFields.description: UTC datetime when event occurred. Required for all events; not calculated.

plainFields.name: source
plainFields.description: Optional – source of this event (e.g., web, mobile, api, batch). Single source only. Example: 'web'.

models.name: ai_shopmall_analytic_profiles
models.description:
Aggregated entity representing a tracked analytic profile (see 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md). 
Implements per-user, per-device, or per-actor analytic tracking profile. 3NF-compliant: ONE profile per entity/actor/session only; links canonical identifier to event records for attribution and analytics.
Business purpose: Normalized index for aggregating events, recommendations, and insights by user, device, or session. No pre-computed aggregations. Example: ID linking customer 313’s browser profile, their relevant events, and analytics. Used as the anchor for event attribution and personalization learning.

Key relationships: Linked to many analytic_events, recommendations, logs, and may reference actor (customer/seller/admin) tables.
Special behaviors: Profile created once; never duplicated. Source-level uniqueness enforced.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique analytic profile ID, unique across all events/links.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Optional – the actor’s ID (customer, seller, admin) this profile is tied to. References the relevant actor/user table, 3NF enforced. Null for anonymous/guest browsing sessions only.

plainFields.name: profile_type
plainFields.description: Type of analytic profile (e.g., user, device, session, guest). Used for separating profiles in personalization use cases. Single atomic value only.

plainFields.name: profile_key
plainFields.description: Unique key for this analytic entity (e.g., browser fingerprint, account UUID, device ID, session token). Uniqueness enforced at model level. Used for linking disparate events into same profile.

plainFields.name: first_seen_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp profile was first initialized. Required; not an aggregate.

plainFields.name: last_seen_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent associated analytic activity. Required; supports profile lifecycle management.

models.name: ai_shopmall_recommendation_logs
models.description:
Audit log for record of AI recommendation delivery and click/interaction results. Implements analytics requirements from 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md for closed-loop recommendation feedback.

Business purpose: Records the actual delivery and interaction status of recommendations to users – for model/algorithm evaluation and A/B testing. 3NF: Each record is an atomic log. Example: Deliver 'product 1001' to visitor 311 at 2025-07-22T14:00Z, logged as displayed and later clicked.

Key relationships: Links to recommendation result (ai_shopmall_ai_recommendations) and analytic_profile (user/session/device identity). Never includes rollup or aggregation data. For reporting only, summary calculations must be in materialized views (mv_*).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique for each recommendation log entry.

foreignFields.name: recommendation_id
foreignFields.description: AI recommendation entry’s {@link ai_shopmall_ai_recommendations.id}. Links delivery to computed recommendation entry. Always required for normalization.

foreignFields.name: analytic_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Identity of the user/session/device for whom log is written. {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_profiles.id}. Required for normalization; 1:N from profile to logs.

plainFields.name: delivery_channel
plainFields.description: Medium/channel recommendation was delivered via (web, push, email, api call). Atomic only. Example: 'web', 'email'.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp recommendation was delivered or shown. Required; always atomic.

plainFields.name: interaction_status
plainFields.description: Atomic status of recommendation outcome: 'displayed', 'clicked', 'ignored', 'converted'. No summaries or aggregate; one per row.

plainFields.name: interaction_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of relevant user interaction (‘clicked’, ‘converted’ etc) if occurred; null if not engaged. Maintains normalization.

models.name: ai_shopmall_ai_alerts
models.description:
AI-generated alerts for fraud or analytics anomalies (see 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md). Implements requirements for alerting on detected business/ops anomalies.

Business purpose: Stores atomic, event-level alert records issued by analytics/fraud/AI layers. No pre-calculated counts by type or user. Example: 'multiple failed logins detected for user 88' or 'payment anomaly on order 1010'. Each row is a single alert occurrence.

Key relationships: Links to analytic_event, analytic_profile, possibly user (actors). Used for alert dashboards, push notifications, compliance audit. Alerts are never denormalized summaries.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique to this alert instance.

foreignFields.name: analytic_profile_id
foreignFields.description: Identity profile linked to this alert entry. {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_profiles.id}.

foreignFields.name: analytic_event_id
foreignFields.description: Analytic event that triggered this alert. {@link ai_shopmall_analytic_events.id}.

plainFields.name: alert_type
plainFields.description: AI/analytic classification of alert (e.g., fraud_suspected, anomaly_detected, policy_violation). Atomic single value only. Never aggregate/rollup.

plainFields.name: alert_message
plainFields.description: Short human-readable message explaining the alert or issue for dashboards or notifications. Single, atomic, fully normalized.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Integer representing alert severity, e.g., 1=info, 2=warning, 3=critical. Fully normalized; do not aggregate by type. Example: '3' for fraudulent payment detected.

plainFields.name: alerted_at
plainFields.description: UTC datetime alert was emitted. Required per row; not a summary.

models.name: ai_shopmall_segmentations
models.description:
AI/analytics-driven segment definitions for the platform – see 06_ai_shopmall_ai_and_analytics_platform.md. Implements user/actor/behavior-based segment records. Each segment defines a rule or cohort for audience analysis and personalized actions.

Business purpose: Defines atomic segments (e.g., "high value buyers", "new users", "churn risk"). Used for targeting by personalization engines and analytics reporting. Maintains 3NF: Each segment row describes a segment with no membership/aggregation data.

Key relationships: Segments can be referenced by other analytics or personalization logic as needed. (User/actor-segment M:N membership should be tracked via a separate table if required.)
Special behaviors: Segment rules/queries stored as code or config, not pre-calculated groups. Naming uniqueness enforced per segment.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique per segment/campaign/audience definition.

plainFields.name: segment_code
plainFields.description: Unique code identifier for the segment (e.g., 'HIGH_VALUE_BUYERS', 'ABANDONED_CART'). Atomic, 3NF enforced by unique constraint.

plainFields.name: segment_name
plainFields.description: Human-friendly segment label. Example: 'High Value Buyers'. Never calculative/aggregated.

plainFields.name: definition
plainFields.description: Rule, SQL, or code snippet that defines the segment logic (e.g., JSON, mini-language). Single value only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of segment definition creation. Audit-only; not an aggregated count.

models.name: ai_shopmall_reviews
models.description:
Product review details - Implements the product review requirements from the Content Review & Engagement document.

Captures customer-submitted product reviews, including star rating, textual feedback, media references, and associated metadata. Fully normalized 3NF structure (all business fields atomic, no redundancies). Example: A customer leaves a review after a successful purchase.

Key relationships: references products via product_id (from already existing Products component), associates to the review writer (customer_id), links to review reports, likes, and engagement logs.
Special behaviors: Only 1 review per customer per product enforced by unique index. Review cannot exist for unpurchased products, enforced at business logic level.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product's {@link ai_shopmall_products.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Review title - Implements review summary. Brief descriptive heading for the review. Ensures normalization; not duplicated elsewhere. Example: "Fantastic, fast delivery!"

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Review body content - Implements reviewer-provided textual feedback. Full review in natural language. Complies with 3NF by storing as atomic value. Example: "Arrived in two days and worked well..."

plainFields.name: rating_value
plainFields.description: Star rating value (e.g., 1-5) - Implements rating aspect of review. Integer representing the customer's evaluation. Ensures normalization, atomic value. Example: 4.

plainFields.name: media_url
plainFields.description: Media attachment URI (optional) - Implements optional media evidence in review. URL to review photo/video. Null if no attachment. Supports normalization. Example: link to image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp - When the review was submitted. Ensures accurate event tracing and normalization. Example: 2025-07-22T12:20:00Z.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last updated timestamp - Reflects last review edit. Ensures auditability. Example: 2025-07-22T12:25:00Z.

models.name: ai_shopmall_review_likes
models.description:
Review likes - Implements the 'like' system for reviews as required in the Content Review & Engagement module.
Represents a customer 'liking' (marking as helpful) a specific review. Enforces single like per customer-review. Maintains 3NF with all atomic fields. Example: Customer likes a review found useful.

Key relationships: References review (review_id), referencing customer (customer_id); no denormalized aggregates.
Special behaviors: Unique index to ensure one like per customer per review.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Target review's {@link ai_shopmall_reviews.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Liker customer {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of like event - Records when like was registered. Ensures audit trail, normalization. Example: 2025-07-22T13:00:00Z.

models.name: ai_shopmall_review_reports
models.description:
Review reporting - Fulfills the report/flagging requirement for moderation in the Content Review & Engagement system.

Represents a user-generated report (flag) on a review, citing violations or problematic content. Enforces 3NF with atomic fields. Example: Customer flags review as offensive.

Key relationships: References review (review_id), reporter (customer_id), links to moderation actions.
Special behaviors: Unique per reviewer per review.

foreignFields.name: review_id
foreignFields.description: Flagged review's {@link ai_shopmall_reviews.id}

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reporter customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for reporting (violation category or free text) - Implements user-provided rationale for reporting. Atomic string, e.g., 'Abuse', 'Spam'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional extended report explanation - Free text. Allows more detail if needed. Normalized. Null if none.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Report created timestamp. For audit and history.

models.name: ai_shopmall_ratings
models.description:
Standalone rating entity - Implements the requirement for storing granular per-entity ratings, decoupled from review text (some flows prefer rating only).

Records a rating value customers give to a product, possibly without textual review. Maintains normalization. Example: Customer gives 5 stars without comment.

Key relationships: product_id, customer_id (from existing tables), can be nullable if only review is present.
Special behaviors: Ensures a customer may rate only once per product (unique index).

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer giving rating {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Rated product's {@link ai_shopmall_products.id}

plainFields.name: rating_value
plainFields.description: Numeric rating value (e.g., 1-5) - Implements atomic score. Normalized. Example: 5.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the rating was made. For event tracing.

models.name: ai_shopmall_questions
models.description:
Q&A questions - Implements the question-asking feature from the Content Review & Engagement document.

Represents a customer's product, order, or general question for sellers/admins (pre-/post-purchase). Maintains normalized 3NF structure. Example: 'How long is the warranty?'

Key relationships: Linked to customer (asker), product being asked about, and answer entity. May be associated to order for post-sale.
Special behaviors: One question can exist per customer per product per subject (business logic).

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Asking customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Subject product's {@link ai_shopmall_products.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Question title. Fulfills inquiry summary requirement. Atomic string. Example: 'Return policy?'.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full question details. Implements main inquiry content. Example: 'Can I return after 14 days?'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Question submission date/time.

plainFields.name: resolved
plainFields.description: Whether the question has been answered (resolved). Maintains normalized status flag. Example: false initially, true after answer posted.

models.name: ai_shopmall_answers
models.description:
Q&A answers - Implements the question answering requirement in the Content Review & Engagement doc.

Stores seller/admin answers to customer questions. Maintains referential link to question and responder. Normalized (one answer per question, all data atomic). Example: Seller responds to return policy Q.

Key relationships: question_id to ai_shopmall_questions, responder_id links to actors.
Special behaviors: Enforces one answer per question per responder.

foreignFields.name: question_id
foreignFields.description: Parent question's {@link ai_shopmall_questions.id}

foreignFields.name: responder_id
foreignFields.description: Responder's actor ID (seller/admin) from related components. Distinction made in business logic.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Answer content - Full text of answer. Normalized field. Example: 'Returns accepted within 30 days.'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of answer post.

models.name: ai_shopmall_comments
models.description:
General-purpose comment entity - Implements the comment feature for reviews, bulletins, and Q&A, following Content Review & Engagement requirements.

Atomic unit for user-generated comments against diverse parent entities (referenced via parent_type+parent_id pattern in application logic). Normalized; all fields atomic. Example: Comment posted under a bulletin or a review.

Key relationships: links to commenter (customer/admin), stores parent type/id for business-layer linking.
Special behaviors: parent_type & parent_id together define the comment target (polymorphic at business level).

foreignFields.name: commenter_id
foreignFields.description: Comment author's ID (customer/admin).

plainFields.name: parent_id
plainFields.description: ID of the parent entity (review, bulletin, question, answer). Implements polymorphic relationship at business logic layer. Not FK-enforced in DB. Example: points to ai_shopmall_reviews.id or ai_shopmall_bulletins.id etc.

plainFields.name: parent_type
plainFields.description: Type of parent entity (e.g., 'review', 'bulletin', 'question', 'answer'). Implements polymorphic relationship handling at business logic level. Normalized: no denormalization of target entity.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Comment content - Implements user comment. Normalized string. Example: 'Thanks for the info!'

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Comment submission timestamp.

models.name: ai_shopmall_bulletins
models.description:
Bulletin entity - Implements platform/community/FAQ bulletin posts as required in Content Review & Engagement.

Represents system, admin, or announcement posts that users can read or comment on. Normalized, all fields atomic. Example: 'System Maintenance on 7/1.'

Key relationships: Author (admin_id), category (category_id), comments via ai_shopmall_comments.
Special behaviors: Enforces category linkage and admin authorship.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category for the bulletin post {@link ai_shopmall_bulletin_categories.id}

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin author {@link ai_shopmall_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Bulletin post title - headline. Normalized. Example: 'Important Policy Update'.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Bulletin post main content. Normalized. Example: Details of the announcement.

plainFields.name: pinned
plainFields.description: Whether bulletin is pinned (shown at top). Fulfills admin pinning requirement. Example: true for urgent/FAQ posts.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Post creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update to bulletin. Allows audit/change tracking.

models.name: ai_shopmall_bulletin_categories
models.description:
Bulletin category - Implements category structure for bulletin posts as specified in Content Review & Engagement doc.

Represents FAQ, system, announcement, or community topic category. Normalized, atomic fields only. Example: 'Announcements', 'Policies'.

Key relationships: Links to bulletins via category_id.
Special behaviors: Category names unique.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name. Implements unique label. Atomic, not duplicated. Example: 'FAQ', 'Maintenance'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Category creation date.

models.name: ai_shopmall_engagement_logs
models.description:
Engagement log - Implements the audit trail and engagement tracking for content interactions.

Stores action logs (view, like, reply, report) for reviews, questions, bulletins, etc. Ensures normalized structure. Example: Customer views review, logs 'view' event.

Key relationships: actor_id (any user), target_entity_id + target_entity_type for polymorphic target.
Special behaviors: Used for analytics and monitoring engagement rates.

foreignFields.name: actor_id
foreignFields.description: Actor performing engagement (customer or admin or seller, depending on target).

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of engaged entity (review, question, etc.). Implements polymorphic reference by business logic.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of engaged entity (e.g., 'review', 'bulletin', 'question', etc.). Normalized for analytics/use-cases.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of engagement (e.g., 'view', 'like', 'reply', 'report'). Atomic, used for analytics.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of engagement event.

models.name: ai_shopmall_moderation_actions
models.description:
Moderation action - Implements moderation and compliance enforcement for community content as required in Content Review & Engagement.

Represents actions taken by admins or automated AI (delete, block, edit, allow). Normalized, all fields atomic. Example: Admin flags review as abuse, action logged here.

Key relationships: moderator_id (admin or automated), target_entity_id/type (polymorphic), links to reports.
Special behaviors: Stores action type, reason, and reference to original report_id if applicable.

foreignFields.name: moderator_id
foreignFields.description: Moderator actor id (admin or AI bot, references already existing actors or systemic users).

foreignFields.name: report_id
foreignFields.description: Original report that prompted moderation ({@link ai_shopmall_review_reports.id}), if applicable. Nullable as not all actions arise from user reports.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of moderated entity (polymorphic, e.g., review, comment, bulletin) - atomic field.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type/name of moderated entity (e.g., 'review', 'comment', 'bulletin'). Normalized.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Action performed by moderator (e.g., 'delete', 'block', 'approve', 'edit'). Atomic, for audit/export/reporting.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Rationale for moderation action. Explains why content was moderated. Atomic. Example: 'Hate speech violation'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Date/time when moderation action was applied.

models.name: ai_shopmall_favorites
models.description: Favorite Entity Mapping Table – Implements multi-entity favorites as required in Favorites & Personalization. Maps each user's favorite items (product, seller, address, inquiry) to their folders with tags and creation audit. Maintains 3NF by referencing all related entities via FKs and storing only atomic relationships, not denormalized info.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each favorite mapping record.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}. Links favorite to actual user (customer).

foreignFields.name: favorite_folder_id
foreignFields.description: Folder's {@link ai_shopmall_favorite_folders.id}. Classifies the favorite entry for organization/grouping.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity being favorited (e.g., product, seller, address, inquiry). Implements multi-entity flexibility per requirements. Normalized as atomic value.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the favorited entity. This flexibly refers to the entity corresponding to entity_type. Fully normalized as reference only. Example: For product favorite, stores product UUID.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the favorite was added. Enables audit and last-access logic as required. Maintains normalization; example: '2025-07-21T13:22:00Z'.

models.name: ai_shopmall_favorite_folders
models.description: Favorite Folder Table – Implements requirement for organizing favorites into folders (custom and default) per customer. Lets users create/delete/rename folders for grouping favorites. 3NF: Folder holds only folder attributes and user reference, not favorite data.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each favorite folder.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}. Links folder to the owning user.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Folder name. User-created identifier for organizing favorites. Ensures normalization by only storing atomic label. Example: 'Wishlist', 'Work Supplies'.

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Indicates if this is the system default folder (true) or a user-created folder (false). Implements business needs for required default folders.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp the folder was created. For audit trail and recovery.

models.name: ai_shopmall_favorite_tags
models.description: Favorite Tag Table – Implements tagging requirements for flexible searching/categorizing of favorites. Each tag is attached to a single favorite and exists as a separate row (3NF). Prevents duplicate tags per favorite.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each tag record.

foreignFields.name: favorite_id
foreignFields.description: Favorite's {@link ai_shopmall_favorites.id}. Links tag to favorited item.

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: Tag value. Short label for categorization/filtering favorites. Fully normalized as atomic string. Example: 'gift', 'eco'.

models.name: ai_shopmall_notification_preferences
models.description: Notification Preferences Table – Implements user-personalized notification settings for favorites/folders. Stores which notification types are enabled/disabled for a favorite or folder; distinguished by target_type. 3NF is maintained by separating notification config from favorites/folder data and indexing by both target_type/target_id and customer.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each notification preference record.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ai_shopmall_customers.id}. Owner of this notification preference.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Scope: 'favorite' or 'folder'. Implements requirement for preference type distinction. Example: 'favorite'.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: Target favorite/folder the preference is for. Ensures referential clarity. For folder scope, stores folder UUID.

plainFields.name: notif_types_enabled
plainFields.description: Comma- or pipe-separated notification types enabled for this object. Implements requirements supporting multi-type (push,email,SMS): e.g., 'push,email'.

models.name: ai_shopmall_permission_roles
models.description: Permission Role Entity - Implements core RBAC security requirements; separates roles from permissions and user assignments, ensuring 3NF and auditable role management.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each permission role record.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Role code - unique, short, for RBAC and API lookups.

plainFields.name: name

### `ai_shopmall_channels`

Channel entity - Implements requirements from the Extensibility & System Structure and System Overview documents. Represents a logical or physical interface/medium (such as web, mobile, kiosk) through which users interact with the AI Shopmall. Maintains 3NF normalization by separating channel metadata from section/business logic. For example, creating a channel entry for 'mobile app' versus 'in-store kiosk'. Key relationships: referenced by sections, configurations, or analytics modules. Special behaviors: Channel codes must be unique and static for integration; deletion is forbidden if referenced by a section or configuration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each channel.
- `code`: Unique short code for the channel (e.g., WEB, MOBILE, KIOSK). For example: 'WEB' for website channel. Ensures normalization by preventing duplicated names/codes in reference tables. Must be unique.
- `name`: Display name of the channel (e.g., Website, Mobile App). Used for user/admin interfaces. Maintains separation of display label from internal codes. For example, 'Mobile App' for the app channel.
- `description`: Detailed description or notes about the channel. For example, specify device compatibility, language restrictions, or features unique to this channel. Nullable as some channels may not require description.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. Implements auditability requirements. Used for tracking the introduction of a channel without inferring meaning from id ordering.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp. 3NF compliance by storing update moment distinctly. Enables audit and rollback operations.

### `ai_shopmall_sections`

Section entity - Implements requirements from Extensibility & System Structure for mapping logical/functional subdivisions within a channel (e.g., Product List, Cart, Admin Panel). Business Purpose: Organizes the system by functionality per channel, enabling extensibility and permission controls. Maintains 3NF by separating sections from business data and meta-configurations. For example, a 'Cart' section in 'Mobile App' or 'Admin Section' in 'Web'. Key relationships: May reference ai_shopmall_channels via foreign key. Special behaviors: Names must be unique within each channel; UI may hide or restrict access by section code.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each section.
- `channel_id`: Belonged channel's [ai_shopmall_channels.id](#ai_shopmall_channels). Enforces that each section is mapped to a specific channel for organizational and permission management purposes.
- `code`: Unique code for the section within the channel (e.g., PRODUCT_LIST, CART) - Implements business logic for UI routing or permission mapping. Ensures no duplicated codes for a channel. For example: 'CART' for the shopping cart section.
- `name`: Display label for the section (e.g., Cart, Orders, Analytics Dashboard). User/admin-facing for menu and navigation. Ensures separation from unique code for human-readable display.
- `description`: Detailed description or business notes for the section - Explains the role or special permissions related to the section. Nullable as not all sections require extended info.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the section was created. Required for audit and rollback, complying with audit log requirements.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_configurations`

Configuration entity - Implements requirements for central configuration storage from Extensibility & System Structure and System Overview. System/business configurations are stored here and optionally scoped by channel/section. Maintains 3NF by separating configuration values from operational data. For example: storing feature toggles, app settings, enablement flags. Key relationships: Optionally references ai_shopmall_channels and ai_shopmall_sections if configs are channel/section-specific. Special behaviors: Code is globally unique unless scoped by channel/section; key lookup supports multilevel fallback (e.g., section > channel > global).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique ID for each configuration entry.
- `channel_id`: Optional referencing channel's [ai_shopmall_channels.id](#ai_shopmall_channels). Distinguishes configs scoped by channel. Nullable to allow global or section-only configs.
- `section_id`: Optional referencing section's [ai_shopmall_sections.id](#ai_shopmall_sections). Distinguishes configs scoped by section. Nullable for channel-level or global configs.
- `code`: Unique configuration code or key (e.g., ENABLE_CART, FEATURE_BULK_UPLOAD). Implements robust settings access pattern. Must be unique for the same channel/section scope. For example: 'PROMO_BANNER_ENABLED'.
- `value`: Configuration value (stringified for flexibility, e.g., true, 10, "feature-x", or JSON). Maintains normalization by keeping one value per config key per section/channel/global context. For example: 'true' for enabled feature, '{"max":5}' for JSON settings. Type parsing/validation is application responsibility.
- `description`: Explanation or business note for the configuration entry (optional). Nullable; for admin-facing context.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp. For historical audits and rollback support.
- `updated_at`: Last modification time.

### `ai_shopmall_attachments`

Attachment entity - Implements the requirements for extensible, versioned file/asset attachments from Extensibility & System Structure. Stores logical references to files used across modules (e.g., product images, manuals, review attachments). Maintains 3NF by separating file reference metadata from file content/data (which is stored in ai_shopmall_files). For example: a product review attachment references the actual blob/file by file_id, but is an independent entity for meta and versioning. Key relationships: References ai_shopmall_files. Special behaviors: Each attachment must have a unique UUID; deletion should check if in use in referencing modules (e.g., reviews, products).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each attachment.
- `file_id`: Referenced file blob's [ai_shopmall_files.id](#ai_shopmall_files). Associates attachment record to physical file/data. Non-nullable for strict referential integrity.
- `entity_type`: Entity table/type code to which this attachment belongs (e.g., PRODUCT, REVIEW, USER, BULLETIN). Implements polymorphic referencing in a normalized way. For example: 'REVIEW' for review attachment. Not a foreign key for normalization separation.
- `entity_id`: Referenced entity's UUID (e.g., productId, reviewId, userId). Enables logical association while maintaining 3NF - the link to target entity is always a UUID. For example: a file attached to review with reviewId = '...'.
- `name`: Attachment display name or label (e.g., 'receipt', 'user-avatar.png'). Used for admin/user preview, can be edited. Not necessarily unique for usage flexibility.
- `version`: Version number of the attachment for update/audit trail. Implements simple version control, preserves old versions for rollback/history. For example, version increments on re-upload of same file for the same entity.
- `created_at`: Attachment creation timestamp. For audit trails and ordering versions.
- `updated_at`: Latest attachment update timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_files`

File entity - Stores and manages the actual binary/file/blob references, as required by the Extensibility & System Structure. Decoupled from attachments for reusability and separation of version/audit logic. Maintains 3NF by not embedding multiple files or blobs, but by linking one file to multiple attachments as needed. For example: image, document, or video file record; may be reused in multiple entities by referencing attachments. Special behaviors: Files should not be deleted unless all referencing attachments are purged; audit logs must record access/modification; URI must be unique.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each file.
- `uri`: Storage URI or blob key, e.g. S3/GCS/MinIO/Local path. Implements file access controls and uniqueness. For example: 's3://bucket/abc123' or 'files/2025/07/img015.png'. Must be unique.
- `name`: Original or assigned filename - For audit and user previews. For example: 'manual.pdf', 'avatar_001.png'. Display only; not required to be unique.
- `size`: File size in bytes. For business rules limiting upload size and for audit. Ensures integrity by reflecting actual data size.
- `mime_type`: MIME type of the file (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Used for preview/render restrictions and validation. Ensures compliance and normalization by not hardcoding type elsewhere.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the file record was created (not when file was uploaded). For audit traceability and storage lifecycle policies.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of latest file info update.

### `ai_shopmall_plugin_modules`

Plugin module entity - Implements the extensibility concept from Extensibility & System Structure, providing the system with a way to reference loaded/available plugin modules by settings and code. Maintains 3NF by centralizing module references apart from operational/setting data. For example, a payment plugin, analytics module, or UI extension module could be represented here. Key relationships: Potential foreign keys (not implemented here) to settings/configuration snapshots. Special behaviors: Codes must be unique and static for integration and dependency resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for plugin module.
- `code`: Unique plugin module code (e.g., 'PAYMENT_STRIPE', 'PROMO_ENGINE'). For internal/programmatic referencing and dependency checks. Must be unique.
- `name`: Display label for the plugin module. Used in admin UIs, module browsers.
- `description`: Detailed description of the plugin/module function. For admin/business notes and integration guidance. Nullable for basic modules.
- `version`: Semantic version string of the plugin/module (e.g., '1.0.0', '2.4.1-beta'). Implements dependency/version compatibility rules. Not enforced by DB, but parsed by application logic.
- `settings_schema`: JSON-schema describing module settings structure. Enables validation and UI generation for module config. Normalization: settings are not stored here, only schema/structure is. For example: '{"type":"object","properties":{"api_key":...}}'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp plugin module was registered.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for plugin module info.

### `ai_shopmall_customers`

Customer Account Entity - This implements the requirements for shopper accounts (AI Shopmall User and Identity Management, Section 3 & 4). Captures unique customer user details (separate from sellers and admins), including registration, status, and relationship to core profile. Maintains strict 3NF normalization by separating role/persona details from profile and authentication. For example, when a new user registers as a customer, this model is used to persist their system identity as a customer only. Key relationships: Links to ai_shopmall_user_profiles (profile), ai_shopmall_user_roles (role claim), and addresses (delivery/contact info). Special behaviors: Role is fixed to 'customer'; can be upgraded (with additional registration) to seller/admin but never mixed at row level.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique customer account UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Belonged user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles). Binds this customer to a core profile with contact and personal info.
- `email`: Customer account's primary email - Implements customer registration requirement; used for contact, login, and notifications. Strictly unique. Example: customer1@example.com. Normalization: atomic, not derived.
- `status`: Current customer account status. Implements activation/ban logic (Section 4). Business meaning: 'active', 'pending', 'banned', or 'deleted'. Used for audit, access management. Ensures atomicity.
- `created_at`: Account creation timestamp - Implements audit and history tracking requirement. Normalization: atomic. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp - Implements modification audit requirement. Updated on every non-read change. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.

### `ai_shopmall_sellers`

Seller Account Entity - Implements requirements for commerce-side actor onboarding (see User and Identity Management, Seller section, seller approval flow). Captures unique seller user records, registration status, approval links, and role isolation. Normalization is maintained by having one core profile per seller, linked with ai_shopmall_user_profiles. When a user applies to become a seller, a record here is created, approval status/state is managed here, and all seller-specific management (stores, inventory) references this entity. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (identity), ai_shopmall_user_roles (role/privilege), ai_shopmall_addresses (business/contact address). Special behaviors: Enforces admin-approval logic, 'pending'/'approved'/'rejected' status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique seller UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Belonged user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `email`: Seller account email - Implements seller registration, notifications, and authentication. Unique per seller. Example: seller42@store.com. Ensures normalized, atomic contact identity.
- `approval_status`: Seller approval workflow status. Implements business process for onboarding ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'banned'). Used for enabling/disabling access. Strictly atomic. For example, on application, set as 'pending', moves to 'approved' when admin confirms.
- `created_at`: Time of record creation. Implements onboarding audit. Updated only on create.
- `updated_at`: Time of last modification. Implements seller management history audit. Updated on profile/permission change.

### `ai_shopmall_administrators`

Administrator Account Entity - Implements privileged user account requirement (Section 3 User Roles, Section 6 Security/Compliance). Captures user-admin records and allows permission management, non-public role tracking, and restricted access to management features. Separation from customer/seller ensures proper RBAC architecture. Only one admin role per person, mapped to ai_shopmall_user_profiles. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (identity), ai_shopmall_user_roles (role binding). Special behaviors: Admin role requires explicit assignation, audit-logged.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique admin user UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Belonged user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `email`: Administrator account's email - Implements privileged login, notifications. Must be unique and official/email domain-restricted. Ensures atomicity. Example: admin@shopmall.com.
- `access_level`: Administrative access scope. Implements compliance between "system", "support", "auditor" or custom RBAC labels. Used to determine admin rights.
- `created_at`: Account creation time. Used for system onboarding audit. Normalization: atomic timestamp. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.
- `updated_at`: Time of last record update (used for edit audit trail, status change).

### `ai_shopmall_user_profiles`

User Profile Entity - Implements centralized profile storage for actor types (Section 5, Profile Management). Stores user's display name, avatar, personal contact data, and preferences in atomic, normalized columns. Shared by all roles via foreign key. Used on registration, OAuth attachment, or when editing personal details. Maintains 3NF by avoiding role-specific fields here. Key relationships: Referenced by ai_shopmall_customers, ai_shopmall_sellers, ai_shopmall_administrators as profile FK. Special behaviors: Only demographic and contact details live here; no credentials or sensitive tokens.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique user profile UUID.
- `display_name`: User chosen display name - Implements personalization and recognition. Example: 'Shopper2025'. Atomic, not derived.
- `avatar_url`: Profile picture URI - Used for personalization/avatar display. Normalized as atomic URI string.
- `phone`: User's contact phone - Used for notification or verification, always atomic. Example: '+82 10 1234-5678'.
- `created_at`: Profile creation timestamp. Implements audit/compliance requirements. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.
- `updated_at`: Profile last modification time - Required for change tracking.

### `ai_shopmall_user_roles`

User Role Entity - Implements role management and escalation/approval logic (Section 7, RBAC design in requirements). Supports assignment of "customer", "seller", "admin", and further role expansions. Normalized mapping between user_profile and current role/permissions. Each actor type row links back to this table to trace privileges. Used on login, permission check, and role upgrade/demotion flows. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (user), referenced by actor tables for RBAC mapping. Special behaviors: One record per user/role combination, unique enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. User-Role mapping UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Associated user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `role`: Role name/type - Implements RBAC claim mapping (e.g., 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', or custom). Atomic. Example usage: grant user 'seller' after approval flow.
- `approved`: Approval status for escalated roles - Implements audit/authorization flow (needed for sellers/admins). True if role is active and operational. Example: False for applicant, True when admin approves escalation.
- `created_at`: Mapping creation timestamp. Maintains audit chain for RBAC. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.

### `ai_shopmall_oauth_accounts`

OAuth Account Link Entity - Implements external authentication connection and OAuth provider profile mapping (Section 4, OAuth). Stores per-user per-provider tokens/accounts. Used when users connect or register via Google, Apple, Kakao, Naver (etc.). Maintains strict separation (1NF/3NF) by not storing private token fields except provider/user/simple metadata. Primary usage: login/registration, plus unlink/refresh token workflows. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (profile FK). 1:N possible (user may have many providers). Special behaviors: Only stores minimal OAuth identity (not actual access token values, for security).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique OAuth linkage UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Associated user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles), owner of this OAuth account.
- `provider`: OAuth provider identifier - Implements provider management (e.g., 'google', 'apple', 'kakao', 'naver'). Atomic, normalized. Used to display serialization/workflow choices.
- `provider_user_id`: Provider-side user identity/claims - Implements mapping requirement. For Google, this is 'sub'; Apple, 'user'; etc. Strictly atomic, never stores tokens.
- `email`: OAuth-linked email - Used to match/verify user identity (never used standalone in customer table; always atomically stored).
- `linked_at`: When this OAuth was attached. Used for timeline and audit purposes. Example: 2025-07-22T13:06:55Z.

### `ai_shopmall_addresses`

User Address Entity - Implements normalized, multi-address management per user (Section 5, Profile, Shipping, Notification addresses). Stores multiple address book entries per user profile (e.g., home, work, recent), avoids denormalization by separating per-address into row. Used at checkout, for shipping/fulfillment automation, and notification preference context. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (foreign FK, owner), reference from order/fulfillment subdomains. Special behaviors: 1 user can have many addresses (1:N), can be tagged 'primary'.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique address UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Owner user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `label`: Address label for recognition - Implements convenience for users managing multiple addresses (e.g., 'Home', 'Work'). Not derived. Atomic.
- `recipient_name`: Recipient's actual name - Used on shipping documents, tracking, etc. Atomic, not derived. Example: 'Kim Minji'.
- `phone`: Recipient/contact phone - Needed for delivery and notification. Only the phone for this address (not user's main phone). Atomic. Example: '+82 10-9876-5432'.
- `postal_code`: Post/zip code of address. Used for quick validation and shipping fees. Atomic. Example: '06109'. Not calculated/derived.
- `address_line1`: Main address line (street address, building). Fulfills shipping and geolocation requirements.
- `address_line2`: Secondary/detailed address (suite, floor, etc.), optional. Atomic, not split.
- `city`: City/locality - Atomic for regional/routing, not derived. Example: 'Seoul'.
- `province`: Province/region/state - Needed for shipping, fees, and legal reqs. Example: 'Gangnam-gu' or 'CA'.
- `country`: Country code/name. Used at checkout for internationalization. e.g., 'KR', 'US', 'JP'. Always atomic.
- `primary`: Whether this is the user's primary/default address. Used for preselecting in checkout/delivery. Only one can be true per user.
- `created_at`: Address record creation time. For audit logs and address history.
- `updated_at`: Address last modification time - Maintains atomic change log for address management.

### `ai_shopmall_sessions`

User/Auth Session Entity - Implements login state, refresh session/cookie management (Section 4, Session/Token Management). Each successful login creates a session, tracks device, expiry, and audit trail. Not holding access tokens directly, only ids/fingerprints/session hashes. Used in multi-device login and concurrent session management. (Atomic, normalized, 3NF.) Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (owner/user). Cross-referenced by audit logs, permission escalations. Special behaviors: Automatic expiry/invalidating on logout/inactivity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique session UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Owner user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `session_token`: Opaque, secure session string (never actual JWT, just system-issued session handle). Used for session validation. Example: 'sess_24U86'.
- `device_fingerprint`: Device/browser fingerprint hash - Used for multi-device security audits. Atomic, not derived. Example: 'fp:hks8l2z18u'.
- `ip_address`: Login IP address. Used for geo-fencing/audit. Example: '175.112.53.14'.
- `expires_at`: Session expiry timestamp. Implements session/hard expiry policies. Example: 2025-08-01T13:06:55Z.
- `created_at`: Session record creation time - Used for session audit trails.

### `ai_shopmall_audit_logs`

User/Actor Audit Log Entity - Implements compliance and traceability (Section 6, Security and Compliance; Section 4 Traceability). Captures every sensitive/critical actor operation: login, logout, permission changes, profile updates, role escalations, etc. Normalized fields: actor_id, event_type, timestamp, detail (atomic/audit-level data). Used for legal/compliance queries, admin/support dashboards. Key relationships: ai_shopmall_user_profiles (actor), ai_shopmall_sessions (session). Special behaviors: System must write a row for every sensitive action, append-only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique audit log entry UUID.
- `user_profile_id`: Actor user profile's [ai_shopmall_user_profiles.id](#ai_shopmall_user_profiles).
- `session_id`: Session during which event occurred. References [ai_shopmall_sessions.id](#ai_shopmall_sessions).
- `event_type`: Log event type - Implements audit categories: 'login', 'logout', 'role_update', 'profile_edit', etc. Used for filtering and compliance queries.
- `event_detail`: Free-form event payload/metadata. Used for investigation/context, always atomic (never derived). Example: JSON string with changed fields, IP, reason, etc.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of audit log entry creation - Immutable; must not be changed after insert.

### `ai_shopmall_products`

Product core entity - Implements the foundational product catalog requirement. Maintains 3NF. Used for product onboarding, search, and AI features. Relationships: variants, images, categories, seller_products, snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each product.
- `code`: Unique product code (SKU). For lookup and onboarding. Unique.
- `title`: Product title for UI and search.
- `description`: Product details and summary.
- `created_at`: Record created time.
- `updated_at`: Record updated time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete marker.

### `ai_shopmall_product_variants`

Product variant/options for multi-SKU. Used in onboarding, inventory, and option display. 3NF.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: Parent product's ai_shopmall_products.id.
- `variant_code`: Unique variant SKU/code.
- `name`: Display name (e.g., Red/Large).
- `attributes`: Serialized KV or JSON for variant attributes (e.g., color=Red;size=L).

### `ai_shopmall_product_images`

Product images/media linking. References product and attachment (file). 3NF.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: Owns ai_shopmall_products.id.
- `attachment_id`: File attachment ref (from ai_shopmall_attachments, systematic domain).
- `ordering`: Ordering for carousel display.
- `created_at`: Create time.

### `ai_shopmall_categories`

Product categories/hierarchies. Enables flexible, multi-deep taxonomy. 3NF. Examples: Electronics, Clothing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`: Self-reference to ai_shopmall_categories.id for hierarchy.
- `code`: Unique category import/search code.
- `name`: Category display name.
- `depth`: Category depth (root=0).
- `ordering`: Ordering among siblings.
- `created_at`: Creation time.

### `ai_shopmall_product_categories`

M:N junction for products and categories. Fully normalized. No denormalized data. Composite unique index enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: Product FK.
- `category_id`: Category FK.
- `created_at`: Assignment timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_inventories`

Stock/Inventory per variant and warehouse. Used for real-time checks and fulfillment. 3NF. No pre-agg data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `variant_id`: Variant tracked (FK).
- `warehouse_id`: Warehouse/location FK.
- `quantity`: Available stock quantity.
- `reserved_quantity`: Held for pending orders, pre-fulfillment.
- `low_stock_threshold`: Threshold for low stock alert.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_warehouses`

Warehouse/physical location for storing goods. 3NF. Used in inventory management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Unique warehouse code (integration, ERP, etc).
- `name`: Display name.
- `address`: Postal/location address.
- `contact_phone`: Warehouse contact (logistics, admin, etc).
- `created_at`: Created timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_seller_products`

Junction for sellers (already in Actors domain) and products. Enforces one seller per product per row (M:N). No denorm. 3NF.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: FK to ai_shopmall_sellers (Actors domain).
- `product_id`: FK to ai_shopmall_products.
- `created_at`: Map assignment timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_sku_barcodes`

SKU-to-barcode mapping for variants, for scanning/OEM use. 3NF. No aggregates/summaries.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `variant_id`: FK to ai_shopmall_product_variants.id.
- `barcode`: Barcode (EAN13, QR, etc).
- `type`: Barcode type format.
- `created_at`: Created timestamp.

### `ai_shopmall_product_snapshots`

Immutable product version snapshot (3NF) for audit/history. Each maps to a product and version number.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: FK to ai_shopmall_products.
- `version_number`: Incremental per-product version number, begins at 1.
- `snapshot_data`: Serialized product spec at point-in-time (JSON, etc).
- `created_at`: When this snapshot was captured.

### `ai_shopmall_carts`

Shopping cart entity - Implements shopping cart management from Order, Cart & Fulfillment. Allows one cart per customer or guest session. Maintains strict normalization and uses proper referential integrity to customers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [ai_shopmall_customers.id](#ai_shopmall_customers). Links this cart to a registered customer. Nullable for guest carts.
- `session_token`: For guest carts: session key; unique among guest carts. Nullable for registered customers.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of cart creation (audit trail).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp; tracks logical deletes for audit/compliance.

### `ai_shopmall_cart_items`

Cart item entity - Each record is a unique SKU in a cart. No denormalization; all calculated data is deferred to materialized views. Enforces uniqueness per SKU per cart.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_cart_id`: Link to parent cart's [ai_shopmall_carts.id](#ai_shopmall_carts).
- `ai_shopmall_product_variant_id`: Link to product variant (SKU) [ai_shopmall_product_variants.id](#ai_shopmall_product_variants).
- `quantity`: Number of units chosen for this SKU. Atomic value; aggregation deferred.
- `selected_options`: JSON string of selected options/properties (e.g., size, color).
- `added_at`: Date/time when added to cart.
- `removed_at`: If removed, timestamp for soft/audit delete.

### `ai_shopmall_orders`

Order record - Business order containing atomic fields only. Each order relates to a cart and a customer. Order number is unique. No denormalized, calculated, or summary fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_customer_id`: Order's customer ref [ai_shopmall_customers.id](#ai_shopmall_customers).
- `ai_shopmall_cart_id`: Order's originating cart ref [ai_shopmall_carts.id](#ai_shopmall_carts).
- `order_number`: Unique order number (ex: ORD-20250722-0001).
- `status`: Status (pending, paid, shipped, completed, cancelled).
- `total_amount`: Order sum at time of order (not updated, not derived from items after order placed).
- `currency_code`: ISO 4217 (KRW, USD etc.).
- `created_at`: Order created at.
- `updated_at`: Order updated at.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_order_items`

Order line item - Each entry is a specific product/SKU/variant at a single price/option at order time. Aggregated data handled in reporting or materialized views only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Parent order reference [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `ai_shopmall_product_variant_id`: Refers to ordered product variant/SKU [ai_shopmall_product_variants.id](#ai_shopmall_product_variants).
- `quantity`: Quantity ordered for this SKU.
- `sale_price`: Price per SKU including discounts at order time.
- `selected_options`: JSON string of selected options/attributes chosen for this item.
- `created_at`: Order item creation time.
- `updated_at`: Order item last update time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_payments`

Order payment record - Each row tracks a payment event. 1:N order to payment allowed (multi-pay/order splits supported). Atomic only, all calculated totals deferred.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Order reference for this payment [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `payment_method`: Payment method code (credit_card, bank_transfer, etc.).
- `status`: Payment status: pending, succeeded, failed, refunded, etc.
- `amount`: Atomic captured/authorized amount for this payment row.
- `currency_code`: ISO currency code for payment (e.g., USD, KRW).
- `external_transaction_id`: Gateway transaction ID (nullable).
- `paid_at`: Timestamp of payment completion (nullable, auditing/forensics).
- `created_at`: When payment was registered (audit record).
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for payment.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for logical delete (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_shipments`

Order shipment record - Tracks an attempted or completed shipment event for an order (partial/combined allowed). Fully normalized. All denormalization/aggregation deferred to reporting layer or views.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Parent order reference [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `shipment_tracking_number`: Unique shipment-provider tracking number (e.g., S123456789).
- `shipment_provider`: Fulfillment/logistics partner (name/code).
- `status`: Current status of shipment (preparing, shipped, delivered, returned, etc.).
- `shipped_at`: When order was picked up/dispatched (nullable, for logistics).
- `delivered_at`: When successfully delivered (nullable).

- `updated_at`: Last modified time for shipment record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (nullable).

Order item return record - Each return request is a separate row, related to order/item/customer (and, if applicable, shipment).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Order ref for returned item [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `ai_shopmall_order_item_id`: Order item ref [ai_shopmall_order_items.id](#ai_shopmall_order_items).
- `ai_shopmall_customer_id`: Requesting customer's ref [ai_shopmall_customers.id](#ai_shopmall_customers).
- `ai_shopmall_shipment_id`: Related shipment (optional, may be null), [ai_shopmall_shipments.id](#ai_shopmall_shipments).
- `status`: Return request status: requested, approved, in_transit, completed, etc.
- `return_reason`: Reason entered by user (e.g., defective, wrong size).
- `customer_comment`: Free-form user note (nullable).
- `processed_at`: If processed, time completed (nullable).
- `created_at`: Initiation time of return.
- `updated_at`: Last status update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete/cancel time (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_refunds`

Order refund record - Tracks atomic refund (partial/multi-refund supported) for an order. All refund fields are auditable and not derived.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Order ref for refund event [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `ai_shopmall_payment_id`: Refunded payment ref [ai_shopmall_payments.id](#ai_shopmall_payments).
- `ai_shopmall_return_id`: If associated with a return, [ai_shopmall_returns.id](#ai_shopmall_returns) (nullable).
- `amount`: Atomic refund value (never derived from order or payment, for auditing).
- `currency_code`: Currency of refund settlement (ISO 4217, e.g., KRW).
- `status`: Refund status (initiated, completed, failed, etc.).
- `reason`: Refund reason (system or user provided, nullable).
- `refunded_at`: If refunded, when settlement completed (nullable).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (audit/compliance).
- `updated_at`: Latest status update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft/cancel delete date (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_order_status_histories`

Order status audit trail - Each change event (status transition) for an order. Never denormalized; only state transitions with reason/comment and audit fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Order ref for which status changed [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders).
- `ai_shopmall_administrator_id`: Admin performing change (nullable), [ai_shopmall_administrators.id](#ai_shopmall_administrators).
- `previous_status`: Prior status value before event (ex: pending).
- `new_status`: Changed status value (ex: paid).
- `changed_at`: Timestamp for transition event.
- `reason`: Human/system-supplied rationale for the change (nullable).

### `ai_shopmall_order_snapshots`

Order snapshot - Immutable image of order state at audit/event time. Used for full audit, rollback, and system state recovery testing. Fully normalized: all calculated/statistical/summary values for reporting must be located only in snapshot JSON. Never written outside audit trigger.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `ai_shopmall_order_id`: Order ref [ai_shopmall_orders.id](#ai_shopmall_orders) snapshot is for.
- `ai_shopmall_administrator_id`: Admin who created snapshot (nullable), [ai_shopmall_administrators.id](#ai_shopmall_administrators).
- `snapshot_type`: Event type for snapshot (e.g., created, paid, shipped, cancelled, returned).
- `order_state_json`: Full JSON snapshot of order/item/payment/shipment states at this event.
- `created_at`: Immutable event timestamp for audit/history.
- `event_trigger`: Which system event or flow caused this snapshot (e.g., checkout, admin_cancel). Nullable for automated/system-level events.
